items.q: Why isn't memory a perfect recording of the past?
items.a: Memory is a **reconstructive mental representation** of the past — *"never always accurate."* Same event → different memories; **high confidence ≠ high accuracy** (metacognition gap). Future imagination also **builds on past memory**.

items.q: What's the difference between seeing and noticing?
items.a: *"Just seeing something many times doesn't mean you'll remember it well."* **Habituation** blinds you to fire extinguishers you've walked past for years. Force a **search** (find the extinguisher) to encode the environment.

items.q: Why does errorful learning beat passive re-exposure?
items.a: **Struggle-then-feedback** wins: draw the **Apple logo** (or penny) from memory first, then look — failure + corrective feedback is the learning signal. *"Then when you look at the logo again, you're going to engage in better learning."*

items.q: Are mnemonics the best way to learn deeply?
items.a: Mnemonics help **arbitrary links** (names like "Happy Henry"). Deeper learning uses **levels of processing**: verbs/interactions, labs, visualization — **semantic depth over shallow labels**. For names, say them aloud and use **retrieval practice**; remembering trust/conversation often matters more than the label.

items.q: Does cognitive aging mean inevitable linear decline?
items.a: Decline is **nuanced and partly malleable**. Some systems decline; others stay stable or improve — **verbal knowledge, selectivity, positivity**. Older adults become **more selective** about what to remember (**socioemotional selectivity** + selective optimization with compensation).

items.q: Can life satisfaction get better with age?
items.a: **Midlife** is often the **lowest** life-satisfaction point; many healthy older adults report a **best-of-life decade**. Book thesis: it can get **better with age** psychologically even as aches rise — aided by an **aging positivity bias**.

items.q: What walking dose grew hippocampal volume in the RCT Castel cites?
items.a: **3–4×/week × ~40 min** aerobic walking → about **+1% hippocampal volume** and better memory at **1 year** vs stretching controls. After ~50 the hippocampus otherwise loses roughly **1–2%/year**.

items.q: Is doing more crosswords enough to stay sharp?
items.a: No — crossword alone mostly **trains a strength**. Maintain sharpness by **strengthening known skills and seeking novelty** (travel, new people, break restaurant/route routines). Add sleep, purpose, social connection, and **positive beliefs about aging**.

items.q: Why does felt age matter more than the calendar?
items.a: After **40**, most people feel about **~20% younger**. **Subjective age predicts longevity better than chronological/biological age**. Challenge stereotypes like *"my knee hurts because I'm old."*

items.q: What did Coach John Wooden say mattered most?
items.a: In Castel's interview: the most important words were **love** and **balance** (physical + life priorities). Model successful agers — grandparents, mentors — and watch for **AI voice scams** that exploit older adults' family-emotion focus.
